question.text: What distinguishes Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) from conventional mutual funds?

answer.text: ETFs allow trading of units throughout the day on stock exchanges
ETFs are actively managed while mutual funds are passively managed
ETFs can only invest in equity instruments
ETFs do not have a Net Asset Value (NAV)

explanation.text: The Logic: ETFs are open-ended mutual funds whose units trade throughout the day on a stock exchange, unlike conventional mutual funds which are bought and sold at the closing NAV of the day. ETF units are mandatorily listed and traded on an exchange platform. The Trap: Option B reverses the typical fact pattern; ETFs do have a NAV and are not restricted to equity instruments. Note: Focus on the source-backed distinction -- intraday exchange trading versus end-of-day NAV transactions. Comparative cost claims about ETF management expenses are not made on the checked source pages.
